Rimanere, salire, tenere: the -g- of vengo

You already know vengo, vieni, viene… vengono. Three very common verbs follow the same pattern.

venire (seen before)rimanere (to stay)salire (to go up)tenere (to keep)
iovengorimangosalgotengo
tuvienirimanisalitieni
lui, leivienerimanesaletiene
noiveniamorimaniamosaliamoteniamo
voiveniterimanetesalitetenete
lorovengonorimangonosalgonotengono

The rule: the -g- shows up with io and loro, and only there. The other persons are regular. Tenere is conjugated exactly like venire: tieni, tiene, with -ie-.

Stasera rimango a casa, ma i ragazzi salgono in terrazza.I'm staying home tonight, but the guys are going up to the rooftop terrace.
Tengo il posto per Anna.I'm saving the seat for Anna.

Don't let the spelling fool you: salire has nothing to do with sailing. It means to go up, and also to get on or into a vehicle. Salgo in macchina: I get in the car. Salgo le scale: I go up the stairs.

", "

Scegliere and bere

Scegliere (to choose) follows the same idea, with a little acrobatic twist: with io and loro, gl becomes lg.

scegliere (to choose)bere (to drink)
ioscelgobevo
tusceglibevi
lui, leiscegliebeve
noiscegliamobeviamo
voisceglietebevete
loroscelgonobevono

Pronunciation: scelgo sounds like “SHEL-go”, scegli like “SHEL-yee”.

Bere is simpler than it looks. The infinitive is short, but every form uses the stem bev- (from the old infinitive “bevere”) plus the regular -ere endings, like prendo, prendi. The rule: conjugate bev- like a regular verb. Forms like “bero” or “beriamo” don't exist.

Che cosa bevi? Io scelgo un analcolico.What are you drinking? I'm going for a non-alcoholic drink.

Just like English (“I drink water”), Italian usually puts nothing before the noun: bevo acqua. Non bevo vino. Bevono acqua frizzante.

title: Bere, rimanere, salire, scegliere
why: After andare, venire, fare, volere and sapere, a few very common verbs are left for going out for a drink. A slow lesson on a single mechanism (the -g- of vengo with io and loro), with review of escono, dovete, so and voglio, the learner's recent mistakes.
